chapter: Wartime South and the Ernie Fields band
title: Ernie Fields band personnel
summary: Singer Melvin Moore, the reed section, pianist Lee Wesley Jones, the ear-learning trombonist Tain and others.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And he had a very, very fine vocalist with this band, Melvin Moore. Great singer. Sing anything. In fact, he was really carrying the band until I got there and helped him carry it. Because when I went, I was playing the lead and most of the solos. In that original reed section, they had John White on one alto, and had... The baritone player was named Sy. And the tenor players were named Lucky... Warren Lucky was one of the tenor player's names; he was from Dallas, Texas -- good saxophone player. And the other tenor player was Gene Montgomery from Fort Worth, Texas. He wasn't there when I first started with the band. He had been to New York to see about some business or something, so he came back and he joined the band.
And we had some fine players with the band, and a fine pianist and arranger, Lee Wesley Jones, who played with the band.

And in the trombone section, we had a trombone player that all I ever knew was Tain! Now, Tain, he couldn't read or write, and he couldn't read music. But if somebody else played it... He was like a computer. If somebody else played... Just like Doc Palmer in Jackson, Mississippi. Tain would listen to somebody else play the lead part, and then from then on he knew it. He played all the leads with the band, in the trombone section, you know.

And we had a fine trumpet player named Jimmy Mitchell; they called him Count. And Parker Berry was one of the trombonists and arrangers. And they had several fine writers writing for the band. It was more or less a territorial band.
